title: There's A River In The Amazon Hot Enough To Cook You Alive
description:

scenes.text: There's a river in the Peruvian Amazon that runs hot enough to cook you alive -- and for years, scientists didn't believe it was real.
Geologist Andres Ruzo grew up hearing about it as a legend from his grandfather. In 2011, he actually went looking for it himself.
It's called Shanay-Timpishka, and it's real -- a six kilometer stretch of river that averages eighty six degrees Celsius, hot enough to seriously injure or kill animals that fall in.
That alone wouldn't be that unusual near a volcano. But the nearest active volcano is over four hundred miles away -- making this one of the largest non-volcanic hot rivers ever documented.
The leading explanation is a fault-fed hydrothermal system -- water sinks deep underground, gets heated by the earth itself, and gets forced back up to the surface through cracks in the rock.
Some researchers think the water may even start as glacier meltwater from the Andes, traveling underground for miles before it ever reaches the surface here. It's still being studied.
Would you have believed a jungle river could actually be hot enough to cook something that fell in?
